extracted.intended_audience: patentees, patent agents, and lawyers practising UK patent law (drafting/assigning/licensing/registering patents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the creation, registration, enforcement and limits of assignments and licences under the UK Patents Acts (principally 1883 and 1888), and on the registration/rectification of patent title information. Covers formalities, typical covenants, rights and defences, compulsory licences, and Patent Office/Comptroller practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied power to assign and license
rubrics_metrics.description: POWER both to assign and to license is by implication given to the patentee by the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that a patent carries an implied right to assign or license; parties should still observe statutory/formal requirements and registration practices discussed below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register assignments and licences promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable to register both assignments and licences as soon as may be after their execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an assignment is not registered an assignee cannot maintain an action for infringement against third parties except licensees from the assignor subsequent to and with notice of the assignment. See Patents Rules 1890 (Rules 67-77) for procedural detail (written request, original document and attested copy to Comptroller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration formalities and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules 67 to 72 prescribe a somewhat complicated system of registry for assignments and licences: a request in writing to the Comptroller, original document and attested copy to be filed; fee of ten shillings payable for each entry; Patent Office refuses to register until patent sealed; deeds must be stamped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Rules exactly: submit originals and attested copies, pay prescribed fees, ensure sealing and stamping to avoid refusal. Rule references and dates (Patents Rules 1890) indicate historical statutory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment must be a deed under hand and seal
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a valid instrument, an assignment ought to be a deed under hand and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft assignments as deeds; include customary covenants (see next item); ensure proper execution formalities to avoid challenges to validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include covenants in assignments (inventorship and validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is usual to introduce into assignments covenants on the part of the patentee that he is the true and first inventor, and that the patent is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider inserting express warranties in sale contracts to avoid the purchaser being left with the patent 'with all its faults' where no fraud or express warranty is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict assignor's power to amend when partial assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the assignor does not part with his entire interest it may be well to insert a covenant binding him not to seek leave to amend the specification or drawings without the written consent of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect assignee's interest by contractually preventing unilateral amendments that might affect scope/rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchaser's duty to search for novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The purchaser ought invariably to have a search made by a competent person at the Patent Office and elsewhere as to the novelty of the invention, prior to his entering into a contract for the purchase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require professional novelty clearance before purchase; this is prudent due diligence to avoid buying worthless patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-owner cannot assign more than his share
rubrics_metrics.description: One of two or more joint patentees cannot assign more than his share of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure assignments specify and reflect only the assignor's proportionate interest; co-owners' rights remain unless conveyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee of a part may sue for infringement of that part
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee of part of a patent separate from other parts may bring his action for an infringement of such part without joining as plaintiffs those persons who have different interests in the other parts, if they have no interest in the damages sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignee of a divisible interest can enforce rights for that interest alone; check case law for nuances on undivided shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee takes subject to known covenants/notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee of the original assignee takes subject to his covenants if he has notice of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure searches and due diligence capture existing covenants and burdens; include express statements in deeds about existing covenants when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of bankruptcy/trustee assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a patentee's bankruptcy, the patent becomes vested in the trustee, who may sue for infringements committed before the bankruptcy; a patentee assigned by trustee may not be estopped from showing the patent is bad for want of novelty in an action brought by the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand distinctions where trustee assignments and insolvency affect estoppel and available defences; consult authorities cited (e.g., Cropper v. Smith).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership rights in patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a partnership at will was formed for the purpose of working an invention previously obtained and registered in the name of one partner, the patent became an asset of the partnership and each partner acquired a right to work the invention; this right was not taken away by the registered owner assigning the patent to a third party who had notice of the partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider partnership arrangements and ensure registration/notice to protect partners' rights; buyers with notice may be bound by partnership equities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buyer bound to take patent with its faults absent warranty or fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: It is no answer to an action to enforce a contract for the purchase of a patent to plead that the patent is worthless or not the novel invention of the plaintiff, there being no proof of fraud and no express warranty; purchaser takes patent with all its faults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include express warranties in sale contracts if buyer requires protection; otherwise buyers assume risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licences may be exclusive/non-exclusive, limited in time, scope, or district
rubrics_metrics.description: Licences have various intents: often for a term shorter than the patent, sometimes not extend to the whole invention, and may be restricted to a particular district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft licences to specify exclusivity, territorial and temporal scope and any field limitations clearly to avoid disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of exclusive licence
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusive licence is one by which the patentee binds himself not to empower any other person to exercise the patent privilege, either at all or within a district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting exclusivity clauses, be explicit about the patentee's covenant and any territorial limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and avoiding partnership by licence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration for a licence is usually an immediate payment or a periodic payment (a certain amount or dependent on extent of use). In the last case care should be taken not to create a partnership when no partnership is contemplated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure royalty and reporting clauses to preserve licensee/licensor relationship and avoid partnership by the parties' actions and profit-sharing arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting covenants in licences (validity, payment, accounts, inspections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee ought to enter into the usual qualified covenants that the patent is valid and that he has a right to grant the licence. The licensee should covenant to pay sums, render properly verified accounts, and allow periodical inspections of books, machinery, stock, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include express covenants on validity and grantability where required; include payment mechanisms, accounting and inspection rights to monitor royalties and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarring licensee from disputing patent validity
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be intended that the licensee should not be permitted to question the validity of the patent or the sufficiency of the specification, recitals should be introduced affirming these points, or express covenants debarring the licensee from raising the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recitals to estop disputing facts at execution; use express covenants to bind future conduct. Note recitals only affirm facts as at execution; covenants can apply to future time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee's defence and effect of recitals/covenants
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of recitals or covenants, a licensee when sued for money reserved by the licence may, where the contract is executory or tainted by fraud, set up that the patent is void as a defence; conversely, a licensee during the continuance of the licence cannot set up that the invention was not new or useful or that the patentee was not the first inventor, or that the specification is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to include non-challenge clauses; be aware of case law nuances (e.g., apportionment where multiple patents are licensed together).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture/determination of licence for breach
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the licence deed may contain no express power of revocation the licensor is entitled to treat the licence as forfeited and to determine it if its terms and conditions have been broken; a simple notice in writing is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prudent to insert a clause giving power to render the licence void in case of non-payment of royalties or non-performance; consider stakeholder clause for royalties during litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignability of licences
rubrics_metrics.description: A licence is not assignable to a third person in the absence of an express or implied power to assign, such as a licence granted to the licensee, his executors, administrators, or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include express assignment/transfer powers where intended; otherwise assignment will likely be ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-grantee consent needed for sub-licence/grant by one grantee
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no clear decision as to the power of one grantee to grant a valid licence without the consent of his co-grantees, but it would probably be held that he cannot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require co-grantee consent in drafting licences involving multiple grantees to avoid invalid grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict licensee from competing outside the patent field
rubrics_metrics.description: As licensees sometimes exercise rights of making or dealing in articles outside the patent under which they are licensed, it may be well in some cases to introduce a covenant restraining them from so doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include non-compete or field-of-use covenants if necessary to protect patentee's wider commercial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirement for licensee-made articles
rubrics_metrics.description: It is frequently stipulated that articles made by a licensee shall be marked in such a way as to show that they were made under the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use marking clauses to identify licensed products and avoid consumer confusion and enforcement problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive licensee covenants (minimum royalties and enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an exclusive licence it is desirable that the licensee should covenant to pay a certain minimum sum at stated periods in the shape of royalty; and in some cases to insert covenants on the part of the patentee to proceed against persons infringing the patent, or to permit the licensee to proceed in the patentee's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiate minimum guarantees for exclusivity and specify enforcement obligations or rights to litigate in patentee's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery when consideration fails; apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a sum of money has been paid for a licence and the consideration fails, the money may be recovered (examples provided). Where a licence covers several patents and one is invalid, failure of consideration may occur if there is no proof of use of the remaining patents and no apportionment of payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include readjustment/apportionment clauses to address partial invalidity or failure of consideration; be aware that annual sums paid for a licence may not be recoverable if patent turns out void except where fraud is proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee cannot dispute validity while licence continues; exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee during the continuance of the licence cannot set up that the invention was not new or useful, or that the patentee was not the first inventor, or that the specification is insufficient; but where a specification's claim is susceptible of two constructions, licensee may insist on the construction making it good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-challenge clauses are generally effective; however, claim construction issues may favour licensee under ambiguous wording. After licence determination, licensee may be able to challenge validity in suits for injunction to restrain infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee's right to ascertain scope of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee has a right to have it ascertained what is the field covered by the specification as properly construed, and is entitled to say that he has not gone inside that field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where boundaries are unclear, seek declaratory proceedings or boundary definition to avoid inadvertent infringement or wrongful payment demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive licensee cannot sue alone; ordinary licensee cannot apply for injunction in owner's name
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusive licensee has no right to bring an action for an infringement in his own name without joining the patentee; an ordinary licensee has no right to apply in the name of the owner for an injunction to restrain infringements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure suits for infringement involve patentee as necessary party; where practicable include express procedural rights in the licence (e.g., permission to proceed in patentee's name).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee restrained from deterring public from dealing with licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee will not be allowed to publish advertisements and circulars calculated to deter the public from dealing with his licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid anti-competitive publicity or conduct directed at licensee's customers; such conduct may be restrained by courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licences: statutory grounds (s.22 Patents Act 1883)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on petition, it is proved to the Board of Trade that, by reason of the default of a patentee to grant licences on reasonable terms, (a) the patent is not being worked in the United Kingdom; or (b) the reasonable requirements of the public with respect to the invention cannot be supplied; or (c) any person is prevented from working or using to the best advantage an invention of which he is possessed, the Board may order the patentee to grant licences on such terms as the Board deems just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know that (i) the three grounds are independent; (ii) Board's orders are final under the Act and enforceable by mandamus; (iii) patents granted before the Act or on pending applications are excepted; (iv) Board may require proof of substantial local manufacture; see Patents Rules 1890 (Rules 60-66) for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and enforcement of compulsory licence orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's orders appear absolute and final with no statutory power to award costs; they may be enforced by mandamus requiring application to the High Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although little used at time of writing, understand administrative remedies and the possible indirect effects (e.g., inducing voluntary licensing or foreign patentees to manufacture locally).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Patents: required entries and evidential effect (s.23 Act 1888)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Register shall contain names/addresses of grantees, notifications of assignments and transmissions of patents, of licences under patents, and of amendments, extensions, and revocations, and such other matters as may be prescribed. The Register of Patents will be prima-facie evidence of any matters directed to be inserted therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all relevant title documents and changes are supplied to Patent Office for entry; certified copies available on payment of prescribed fee. Copies of deeds/licenses must be supplied in prescribed manner for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's duty to enter proprietor on proof of title (s.87)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person becomes entitled by assignment, transmission or other operation of law to a patent, the Comptroller shall on request and on proof of title to his satisfaction cause the name of such person to be entered as proprietor in the Register of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare proof of title documents to the Comptroller; once entered the registered proprietor has power to assign, grant licences, give receipts and deal with the patent subject to registered rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of trusts not to be entered (s.85)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of trusts, expressed, implied, or constructive, are not to be entered in the register nor to be received by the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where equitable interests exist, parties must enforce them by other means; trust notices cannot be relied on via the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probate/administration must be registered to complete title chain
rubrics_metrics.description: The probate of a patentee's will or the letters of administration must be registered in order that when the executor, administrator, or legatee comes to deal with the patent the chain of title may be complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File probate/letters promptly to ensure clear title for subsequent dealings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of register and Comptroller corrections (s.90, s.91)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may, on application of a person aggrieved by omission or wrongful entry, make orders for making, expunging or varying entries and decide necessary questions; the Comptroller is empowered to correct clerical errors in names/addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use court proceedings for substantive rectification; apply to Comptroller for clerical corrections. Court may direct notice to Comptroller and require office copy of order be left at Patent Office (Rule 74).

rubrics_metrics.name: False entries are misdemeanours (s.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: The making of false entries in the register, making any writing falsely purporting to be a copy of an entry, and tendering any such writing in evidence are declared to be severally misdemeanours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accuracy and honesty in documents submitted to the register; falsehoods carry criminal exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and certified copies of the register (s.114, s.88)
rubrics_metrics.description: The register is to be open at convenient times to public inspection (subject to regulations); certified copies sealed with Patent Office seal of any entry will be given on payment of fee. Former registers are to be deemed parts of the new register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public inspection and obtain certified copies when checking title; remember earlier registers remain effective parts of the record.
